title: Amazon White Background Photo Requirements: 2026 Checklist
description: Prepare an Amazon MAIN image with a pure white RGB 255 background, correct product coverage, clean edges, and a reusable export workflow.

blocks.text: An Amazon MAIN image needs more than a background that looks white on your screen. The background should be pure white RGB 255, 255, 255, the product should fill at least 85% of the frame, and the image must avoid text, logos, borders, watermarks, or extra graphics. Category-specific rules can add exceptions, so Seller Central remains the final check before upload.

Quick answer: create one clean transparent master, place it on a true-white canvas for Amazon, then inspect the edge and crop before export. This separates background removal from marketplace formatting and makes future variants easier to produce.
Amazon MAIN image checklist

blocks.caption: Practical checklist reviewed against Amazon guidance on September 8, 2026. Exact category requirements can override these general rules.

cells: Background
Pure white RGB 255, 255, 255 for the MAIN image
Sample several corner pixels with an eyedropper; do not judge white by eye alone.
Product coverage
Product fills at least 85% of the image area
Keep a small safety margin and make sure no product edge is accidentally cropped.
Image content
Show the actual product; avoid text, logos, borders, watermarks, and background graphics
Remove promotional badges and any prop that could be mistaken for an included item.
Dimensions
500–10,000 px on the longest side; Amazon recommends more than 1,000 px on each side for zoom
Start from a sharp original and export at 1,600 px or larger when the source supports it.
File format
JPEG, TIFF, PNG, or non-animated GIF
Use a high-quality flattened JPEG for a straightforward white-background MAIN image; keep the transparent PNG as your private master.
Image quality
Clear, unpixelated, and free of jagged edges
Inspect at 100% zoom for blur, halos, missing parts, and compression damage.

blocks.caption: Background removal is the middle step, not the final marketplace file. Inspect the cutout first, then create a separate flattened white-background export for Amazon.

blocks.text: Need the complete browser-local cutout process first?
blocks.label: Follow the product-photo background removal workflow

blocks.text: Five-step workflow without a studio
1. Shoot for a clean edge, not a perfect white backdrop

Use soft, even light and a background that contrasts with the product. A phone, a stable support, white foam board, and window light are enough for many small products. Avoid busy carpet or fabric when it blends into thin product edges.
2. Remove the original background

Create a transparent cutout and inspect difficult areas such as handles, chains, hair, glass, mesh, and gaps between product parts. AI is a fast first pass, but a seller remains responsible for checking the result.
3. Place the cutout on true white
Add a solid RGB 255, 255, 255 canvas behind the cutout and flatten the marketplace copy. Keep the transparent PNG separately; transparency itself is not the same as an Amazon white background.
Not sure why a transparent PNG and a white-background image are different?
blocks.label: Read the transparent PNG guide

blocks.text: 4. Crop to the product, with a safety margin

Scale the product so it fills at least 85% of the frame while preserving every part. The correct crop depends on the shape: a tall bottle, a wide bag, and a multi-piece set should not be forced into the same margins.
5. Export and run a 100% inspection

Export from the original-resolution source rather than enlarging a small screenshot. Check the white corners, edge halo, sharpness, crop, color, and included-product accuracy. Then compare the final file with the current rule shown for your category in Seller Central.

blocks.text: Common reasons a MAIN image still fails

items.label: The background only looks white
items.text: Lighting can turn paper gray, yellow, or blue. Verify pixel values after export.

items.label: A white or colored halo remains
items.text: Inspect around curved and reflective edges at 100% zoom.

items.label: The product is too small or clipped
items.text: Meet the frame-coverage rule without cutting off handles, caps, or bundled parts.

items.label: The image implies extra items
items.text: Remove props, badges, and packaging elements unless they are genuinely included and permitted for the category.

items.label: The file is soft or enlarged
items.text: Return to the original photo instead of scaling up a compressed file.

items.label: The category has an extra rule
items.text: Apparel, books, jewelry, multipacks, and other categories can have requirements beyond the general checklist.

items.question: Does an Amazon MAIN image need a pure white background?
items.answer: Amazon's general MAIN image guidance specifies a pure white background with RGB values 255, 255, 255. Check Seller Central for category-specific requirements before uploading.

items.question: Is a transparent PNG the same as an Amazon white background image?
items.answer: No. A transparent PNG has no background pixels. For the Amazon MAIN file, place the cutout on a solid RGB 255 white canvas and export a flattened marketplace copy.

items.question: How large should an Amazon product image be?
items.answer: Amazon currently accepts images from 500 to 10,000 pixels on the longest side and recommends more than 1,000 pixels on each side for zoom. A 1,600-pixel-or-larger export is a practical target when the source is sharp enough.

items.question: Can the Amazon MAIN image contain text or a logo?
items.answer: The general MAIN image rules prohibit added text, logos, borders, watermarks, and other graphics. Use secondary images for explanatory callouts when the category permits them.

items.question: Can I use the same white-background image on other marketplaces?
items.answer: Often yes, but image dimensions, transparency handling, crop behavior, and overlay rules vary. Keep one transparent master and create a checked export for each channel.
